transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I start out really motivated, but I keep zoning out when people explain what to do and end up not finishing my class assignments or business tasks the way they were asked. It's really starting to make it hard to keep up with my college courses and run my online shop.

Have these focus and follow-through problems been present since childhood, or did they start more recently along with feeling down, losing interest, or feeling especially anxious? Also, do they happen even when your mood feels okay?

They've actually been around since elementary school, when my teachers complained about me constantly getting out of my seat and my parents called me a wind-up toy. While it got much worse about two years ago with college and my shop, it happens all the time, even when my mood is perfectly fine and I'm not feeling down or anxious at all.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a longstanding pattern since elementary school of inattentive symptoms (zoning out when given instructions, not finishing assignments/tasks as asked) along with childhood hyperactive behavior (constantly getting out of seat, described as a 'wind-up toy'). Symptoms persist across settings and currently impair academic and occupational functioning. They are not limited to episodes of depression or anxiety, supporting ADHD, predominantly inattentive presentation/hyperkinetic disorder.
